Judgment And Award Dated 25.11.2021 Passed In Mvc

Small Causes, Member, Prl. Mact, Bengaluru Scch-1,
Partly Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation
And Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
Oral Judgment
Heard Sri.Chikkanna.C, learned counsel for the appellant who appears physically before this Court.
Also heard Sri.S.V.Hegde Mulkhand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 who appears through video conference.
2. Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in M.V.C. No.4310/2019 dated 25.11.2021.

entities.text: Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The appellant who sustained injuries in a road traffic accident filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- in total.
The tribunal through the NC: 2024:KHC:37763 impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.1,77,200/- as compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed.
4. Sri.Chikkanna.
C, learned counsel for appellant, arguing the matter, contends that the appellant sustained fracture of patella which is a grievous injury.
He took treatment as inpatient and during the course of treatment, he underwent surgery.
The appellant as a labourer cum loader was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
However, the tribunal taking the notional income as Rs.12,000/- per month, awarded meager sum as compensation under the head loss of future earnings.
Learned counsel states that a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- is required to be awarded in addition to the sum that is granted by the tribunal as compensation.

5. Vehemently opposing the submission thus made, learned counsel Sri.S.V.Hegde Mulkhand contends that the tribunal taking into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case,
awarded justifiable sum as NC: 2024:KHC:37763 compensation and thus the appeal itself is not maintainable.

6. The tribunal, subjecting the evidence of PW-1 and 2, Ex.P-5 to P-15 to scrutiny came to a conclusion that the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,77,200/- as compensation divided under following heads:-

sentences.text: Pain and sufferings 40,000-00

Medical expenses 26,600-00 Food and nourishment, 27,000-00 attendant charges Transportation charges 2,000-00 Loss of future earning 57,600-00 capacity due to permanent disability Loss of income during 24,000-00 treatment and rest period

As rightly submitted by Sri.S.V.Hegde Mulkhand, having considered the nature of injuries sustained and the findings given with regard to the disability, the tribunal awarded justifiable sum under all heads.
However, the tribunal failed to award any amount as compensation towards loss of amenities in life.
The appellant was aged about 68 years by the date of accident.
The amount of pain the appellant would have suffered due to fracture of patella can be imagined.
Also there is a clear mention that his right knee flexion restricted.

Having considered these facts and as no amount is awarded under the head loss of amenities in life, this Court is of the view that in addition to the sum that is awarded by the tribunal as compensation, the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- globally.

9. Thus, in the light of the said finding, the appeal is disposed of with the following:-
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The compensation that is awarded by the Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru through NC:
2024:KHC:37763 orders in M.V.C. No.4310/2019 dated 25.11.2021 is enhanced by Rs.50,000/-
iii.

entities.text: Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv. The 2nd respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
v. On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the same.
vi. The order of pay and recovery remains intact.
